formal_definition: In the UK, e-money is defined, for the purposes of the Bank of England PRA's 18 May 2026 Dear CEO letter on deposits, e-money and stablecoins, by reference to the Electronic Money Regulations 2011 (SI 2011/99) as electronic monetary value the customer holds as a claim against the issuer. E-money issuance is a regulated activity separate from deposit-taking; the PRA's letter treats e-money, like stablecoin issuance, as carrying different (non-FSCS) protections from a bank deposit, and expects deposit-taking banking groups that also issue e-money or stablecoins to retail customers to do so from a separate, insolvency-remote, distinctly-branded entity. Other jurisdictions regulate e-money under their own separate regimes, not covered here.
plain_definition: Digital value stored electronically and redeemable at face value on request -- the sort of balance behind many prepaid cards and non-bank payment apps -- which is legally distinct from a bank deposit even though it can look and feel similar to a customer. Because it is not a deposit, it typically does not carry the same government-backed protection if the issuer fails.
